stores.title: The things you cannot afford to lose, or to leak.

items.title: Secrets
items.desc: Seed phrases, keys and account numbers: the small values that unlock everything else. Hidden until you ask for them.

items.title: Passwords
items.desc: Sites, usernames and passwords, saved and filled by the browser extension.

items.title: Notes
items.desc: Short text for quick thoughts and private details, kept in tabs.

items.title: Documents and spreadsheets
items.desc: Write long-form text in a rich text editor and have it sync across your devices as you type, encrypted end to end. The server stores and forwards sealed changes and merges nothing. Encrypted spreadsheets sync across your devices too.

drive.title: Drive and safe sharing
drive.desc: Upload any file into folders, with a Trash that keeps deleted items for a while. Send an item or file to another Zekke user, and the server relays a blob it cannot open.

how.title: Your device does the sealing. The server only holds the result.

steps.title: Your browser makes a phrase
steps.desc: It generates a 12- or 24-word BIP39 recovery phrase on your device. Your account address and root keys are derived from it locally. Nothing is sent.

steps.title: Every item gets its own key
steps.desc: Each item key is random and generated on your device. It is wrapped under a random key for that kind of data, and that key is wrapped to your phrase and to each device that holds it.

steps.title: The server gets a sealed blob
steps.desc: Plus the little that routing needs: its size and when it changed. No master key, no recovery database, no support tool that can open a vault.

steps.title: Type the phrase anywhere
steps.desc: Typing the phrase in a new browser enrols it as a device and restores the whole vault. Each device has its own keys and its own 6-digit device PIN, which unlocks them.

security.title: Zero-knowledge by construction, not by policy.
security.subtitle: Zekke cannot read your data, even under legal compulsion, because it never holds a key that could decrypt it.

standard.title: Standard mode
standard.desc: The recovery phrase alone protects the account, and each device has its own 6-digit device PIN. The server counts every guess without ever seeing the PIN. After ten wrong tries, that device forgets the account until you type your phrase again. You can upgrade to Paranoid at any time, from Settings.
standard.bestFor: Best for: most people. It is the default and the recommended choice.

paranoid.title: Paranoid mode
paranoid.desc: Two things protect the account: your recovery phrase and a 6-digit account PIN. Adding a device with your phrase, removing devices and deleting the account all need the account PIN, so a stolen phrase cannot do any of them. Paranoid cannot be turned off, and a forgotten account PIN ends the account.
paranoid.bestFor: Best for: people who fear their phrase being found or copied, and accept the risk of forgetting the account PIN.

lose.title: Lose the phrase, lose the vault.
lose.desc: Nobody, including Zekke, can restore access. You verify your copy of the phrase at sign-up and receive a printable recovery kit. A lost device is different: remove it from another device or with your phrase, and the keys it held are rotated.

postQuantum.title: Post-quantum where it counts
postQuantum.desc: Data at rest uses AES-256-GCM, which is considered resistant to known quantum attacks. Sharing between accounts uses PQXDH, a hybrid of X25519 and ML-KEM-768, so an attacker must break both a classical and a post-quantum algorithm.

specs.title: The cryptography, named.

sections.title: 1. Introduction
sections.content: Welcome to Zekke! The services are operated by Cryple LLC, located at 30 N Gould St Ste R, Sheridan, WY 82801, USA. We respect your privacy and are committed to protecting your personal data. This Privacy Policy will inform you as to how we look after your personal data when you visit our website.

sections.title: 2. Data We Collect
sections.content: Currently, through our landing page, we collect only your email address when you sign up for our early access waitlist. Emails are securely handled by our third-party provider, Loops.so.
sections.note: No name, IP, region, device, or other data is being kept by Zekke. However, an IP address may be retained permanently if you are engaged in activities that breach our Terms of Service (e.g., spamming, DDoS attacks against our infrastructure, brute force attacks).

sections.title: 3. How We Use Your Data & Account Linking
sections.content: We use the data we collect for the following purposes:
items: To notify you when Zekke is ready for public or beta access.
To send you important updates regarding our platform’s development.
We do not sell, rent, or distribute your email address to third parties.
sections.extra: Importantly, an account on the future Zekke App will not have a linked email by default. The email you provide on our waitlist will not be related to the account you eventually create.
sections.extra2: For support interactions, your email will be kept solely in our email server in order to assist you and clarify information. We will not link your email to your app account unless we introduce this feature in the future and you explicitly and voluntarily choose to add an email to your account.

sections.title: 4. Data Security & "Zero-Knowledge"
sections.content: The Zekke App, when launched, will keep only encrypted data from users and manage the encrypted storage. Because of this "Zero-Knowledge" architecture, we cannot read your stored encrypted files or passwords. Standard waitlist emails collected on our marketing site are handled securely by Loops.so.

sections.title: 1. Zero-Knowledge Architecture
sections.content: Zekke is built from the ground up as a zero-knowledge service. Our architecture means that no employee, administrator, or attacker compromising our servers can read your stored items, credentials, notes or documents.
sections.note: We operate strictly under the following policy:
items: Your recovery phrase and your PIN never leave your browser.
All encryption/decryption happens locally on your device before transmission.
We only store randomly generated salts, ECDSA public keys, and encrypted payloads.

sections.title: 2. Cryptography Practices
sections.content: We leverage industry-standard cryptographic tools:
items: Authentication: ECDSA P-256 signatures over a client-generated challenge; in Paranoid Mode the PIN is stretched client-side with PBKDF2-SHA256 (600,000 iterations) and stored server-side as an Argon2id hash.
Signing: Asymmetric public/private key-pairs (ECDSA P-256) are derived client-side from your recovery phrase and sign every challenge and privileged action.
Data Storage: vault items, notes and documents are encrypted on the client device using AES-256-GCM, each under its own key.

Post-Quantum: the hybrid PQXDH construction — X25519 combined with ML-KEM-768 — is implemented and specified for encrypting to another person. Private sharing is the feature that will use it; it is not shipped yet.

sections.title: 3. Infrastructure Protection
sections.content: Our server infrastructure is protected by rigorous engineering limits against attack vectors:
items: Single-use nonce locking prevents replay attacks on every authentication and privileged action.
Database volumes and object storage buckets are encrypted at rest via our cloud providers.

Rate limiting on authentication endpoints is designed and not yet deployed. Until it is, a 6-digit PIN in Paranoid Mode is defended by server-side cost alone, and we would rather say so than imply a control we do not run.

sections.title: 4. What This Model Does Not Cover
sections.content: A security policy that lists only strengths is marketing. These are the limits of our architecture, stated plainly, so you can weigh them before you rely on us.
sections.note: Each of these is a known and accepted limitation of the current design, not an oversight:
items: Data availability. Your encrypted data lives in our storage. We cannot read it, but we do hold it: if our storage were lost or withheld, the ciphertext would go with it. Zero-knowledge removes our ability to read your data; it does not remove our custody of the bytes. Keep your own copy of anything you cannot replace.

Metadata. We cannot see what you store, but we can see that you store: how many items exist, roughly how large they are, and when they changed. Encrypting content is not the same as hiding activity, and we do not claim to hide it.

Losing your phrase is final. There is no recovery path, so there is nothing for an attacker to subvert and nothing for a court to compel — and equally nothing for us to offer you if the phrase is gone. This is the trade, stated once and honoured in both directions.

sections.title: 5. Auditing & Open Source
sections.content: We believe security requires transparency. Therefore, our target is an "Open Source Client" philosophy, meaning all client-side decryption logic is inspectable by security researchers before usage.
sections.note: We are presently undergoing internal security reviews ahead of formal independent third-party penetration testing.

sections.title: 6. Vulnerability Disclosure
sections.content: If you discover a security issue or vulnerability please report it immediately rather than disclosing it publicly. We are working on a Bug Bounty program, but in the meantime please contact our security team.

sections.title: 7. Contact Information
